_comment: Adaptive growth-strategy configuration (owner direction, 2026-08-02). Mutable operating policy toward the 100k-subscriber objective — separate from config/channel.json (static brand/style identity) and config/gates.json (safety/quality gates, which this file must never duplicate or override). Agent 0 may edit this file's mutable fields when evidence supports it, following the Controlled Self-Modification Loop in agents/0_orchestrator.md's Growth Strategy section. Every edit here should be paired with an experiment_ledger entry in state/performance_notes.json explaining why.

objective.note: A stretch objective, not a guaranteed forecast (owner direction, 2026-08-02). Pacing math is descriptive, never a promise.

trajectory_status_thresholds.note: GREEN >=90% of required pace to the next checkpoint, AMBER 70-89%, RED <70%. A RED classification must trigger a system-level diagnosis in the next analytics cycle, never an automatic volume increase (agents/0_orchestrator.md Growth Strategy section).

current_production_allocation.reason: Direct owner instruction, 2026-08-03 — not a system-diagnosed self-modification, so the evidence-level gating below does not apply to this specific change (it applies to changes Agent 0 initiates on its own from analytics; a direct owner instruction is always authoritative). Cadence allocation (5 shorts + 2 long-form/day) is unchanged, but the PRODUCTION SCHEDULE was corrected 2026-08-04: owner reported the 'produce the whole week on Monday' batch model was 'messing with the system' (real concurrent-agent id/title collisions, and — the more serious problem — content sat gated in ready_to_publish without ever actually being published for days). Each day's 5 shorts + 2 long-form are now produced AND published/scheduled on that same day, not ahead of time — see config/channel.json.publishing_schedule.daily_production_mode and agents/0_orchestrator.md's 'Daily content cycle' section (renamed from 'Weekly batch cycle').

A.description: Original starting baseline. Retired 2026-08-03 in favor of F.

B.description: Shorts-only on selected days, long-form on selected days only — requires repeated_pattern evidence that Shorts materially outperform long-form on subscriber/engagement value.

C.description: One slot reserved for stronger experimentation or no publish — requires evidence that a lower-volume, higher-bar approach improves quality/conversion.

D.description: Weekday-dependent allocation based on verified cadence performance — requires repeated_pattern cadence evidence.

E.description: Controlled expansion above 4 total daily uploads — requires verified quota headroom (real test, not assumption), strong_channel_pattern evidence of demand, and zero quality/fatigue degradation. Historical precedent: ~11 uploads in an hour triggered uploadLimitExceeded once — never assume >4/day works without a real, minimal, reversible test.

F.description: Current allocation (owner direction, 2026-08-03). All 7 total uploads/day still fall within the verified-safe ~4-11/day range only if the PUBLISHING phase stays throttled and spread across the day/week per publishAt scheduling — the per-upload uploadLimitExceeded check is unchanged and non-negotiable regardless of this allocation.

evidence_requirements.high_risk_change: strong_channel_pattern or a clearly exceptional single event (breakout, policy risk, quota failure, credential failure, corrupted state) required
evidence_requirements.note: See agents/0_orchestrator.md's Analytics Intelligence protocol for the full evidence-level definitions (observation/early_signal/repeated_pattern/strong_channel_pattern) — this section only maps evidence levels to the change-risk levels below, it doesn't redefine them.

low_risk: upload spacing within existing slot count
medium_risk: swapping one daily format slot for another
high_risk: changing several production stages at once

breakout_thresholds.note: Ratios of a video's age-normalized views to its same-format median (analytics_intelligence.format_baseline()). Never compare Shorts to long-form directly. Agent 0 may adjust these as the channel matures and sample sizes grow — record any change in the experiment ledger.

fatigue_thresholds.note: Unchanged from the existing system — see analytics_intelligence.FATIGUE_SHARE_THRESHOLD (0.30) and FATIGUE_CONSECUTIVE_THRESHOLD (3). Referenced here, not duplicated, so there is one source of truth.

quota_aware_limits.account_verification_status: Owner-confirmed 2026-08-04: the channel's YouTube account is verified with advanced features. YouTube's public daily upload limits are roughly 10-15 videos/day for new/unverified accounts vs. 50-100/day for verified accounts with advanced features — this account sits in the higher tier.
quota_aware_limits.real_world_confirmation: 2026-08-04: uploaded all 7 of a day's items (5 shorts + 2 long-form) back-to-back in one sitting with zero uploadLimitExceeded errors — confirms 7/day is comfortably within this account's real quota, not an untested middle zone.
quota_aware_limits.verified_failure_point: ~11 uploads within about an hour of wall-clock time triggered HTTP 400 uploadLimitExceeded on 2026-07-27, before the account's verified status/tier was confirmed — publishAt scheduling does not protect against this, only the upload call's own timing matters. Left here as reference, not as an active ceiling.
quota_aware_limits.note: Owner direction 2026-08-04: this is informational context, not an enforced pre-emptive cap — don't artificially slice/defer uploads to stay under an old assumed number (the previous 4/day framing predated confirming the account is verified and predates the successful 7-in-one-sitting real-world result above). The per-upload uploadLimitExceeded check in the PUBLISHING/Daily content cycle step remains active as a cheap real-time safety net regardless — it reacts to what the API actually says rather than a guessed number, so keep it; just don't treat any specific daily count as a wall to preemptively stop at.

rollback_policy.note: Every medium/high-risk change must define its own rollback condition at implementation time (agents/0_orchestrator.md's Controlled Self-Modification Loop). This file's current_production_allocation.previous_production_allocation field is the mechanical rollback target for allocation changes specifically — set it to the outgoing allocation whenever current_production_allocation changes, never leave it stale.
rollback_trigger_examples: subscriber growth materially declines vs. the pre-change baseline
content quality falls (gate failures, owner feedback)
the change produces no benefit after its evaluation window

content_portfolio_default.note: Default mix — Agent 0 may adjust temporarily per situation (e.g. 50/30/20 with no winners yet, 70/25/5 validating a clear winner, 50/40/10 under fatigue, 75/20/5 in stable strong growth). Record any deviation and its reason in the relevant cycles[] entry.
